artifact.canonical_name: Deterministic Task Scheduling in In-Vehicle Networks for Software-Defined Vehicles

sources.title: Deterministic Task Scheduling in In-Vehicle Networks for Software-Defined Vehicles
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors propose deterministic task scheduling for SDV in-vehicle networks with centralized/zonal compute and compare it with shortest-path and minimum-execution-time approaches.
The abstract reports better deterministic-service guarantees, support for increasing computational workloads, and more balanced workload/resource utilization across IVN nodes.
The evaluation covers multiple IVN topologies and hybrid wired/wireless implementations.

limitations.text: The accessible primary abstract does not expose scheduling formulation, topology sizes, task/deadline distributions, deterministic-service metric, wireless parameters, numerical gains, or computational complexity.
The abstract's hybrid wireless-wired result should not be generalized to production IVN reliability/safety without detailed channel and interference assumptions.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Deterministic Task Scheduling in In-Vehicle Networks for Software-Defined Vehicles; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The primary abstract verifies the deterministic scheduler, comparison objectives and multi-topology/hybrid-wired-wireless evaluation scope, but not the numerical setup/results.

unresolved_questions: Inspect the full paper for task/network model, hard-deadline metric, topology sizes, numerical comparison results, wireless assumptions, and solver/runtime complexity.

editorial.why_now_note: Centralized/zonal E/E turns function placement and network path selection into a coupled scheduling problem; deterministic resource governance is therefore architecture-relevant.
editorial.rationale: Highly relevant candidate in principle, but quantitative scheduler evidence must be inspected before inclusion.
